title: Mauritania National Olympiad
text:
The Mauritania National Mathematics Olympiad (French: Les Olympiades Nationales de Mathématiques) is the premier mathematical competition in Mauritania. It is organized by the National Committee for Mathematics and Science (Mawahib) under the auspices of the Ministry of National Education.

The competition was officially established in its current format in 2017 and aims to identify and nurture mathematical talent across the country's 15 regions (Wilayas).

Contents

  • 1 Competition Format
    • 1.1 1. The Rallye (Rallye National de Mathématiques)
    • 1.2 2. The Olympiad (Olympiades Nationales)
  • 2 Level and Syllabus

Competition Format[edit]

The competition is divided into two main categories based on the educational level, recently undergoing a transition due to educational reforms.

1. The Rallye (Rallye National de Mathématiques)[edit]

Targeted at middle levels (currently transitioning to 2nd, 4th, and 5th years of secondary school).

  • Round 1 (First Tour): A Multiple Choice Question (MCQ) exam.
    • From 2017–2023: 25 questions (30 questions in 2017).
    • Current format (2024): 20 questions in 60 minutes.
  • Round 2 & 3 (Regional & National Finals): A team-based speed competition. The top 3 students from each of the 15 Wilayas form a team. Teams compete in regional hubs.
    • Format: 10 MCQ questions, with only 90 seconds per question.

2. The Olympiad (Olympiades Nationales)[edit]

Targeted at terminal years (currently 4th and 7th year, transitioning to 3rd Prep and 6th Secondary).

  • Advancement Criteria: To qualify for subsequent rounds, a student must:
  1. Score at least 25/100.
  2. OR be among the top 5 students in their Wilaya.
  3. OR have participated in the 3rd round of the "Rallye" in the previous year.
  • Exam Format: Unlike the Rallye, the Olympiad focuses on descriptive, proof-based problems covering Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory.

Level and Syllabus[edit]

The level of the competition is designed to challenge students' logical reasoning and problem-solving skills.

  • Junior Levels: Focuses on mental arithmetic, basic geometry properties, and logical puzzles (MCQ format).
  • Senior Levels (Olympiad): Involves advanced topics such as:
    • Algebra: Nested radicals, functional equations, and inequalities (e.g., Cauchy-Schwarz applications).
    • Geometry: Euclidean geometry proofs and properties of triangles and circles.
    • Number Theory: Divisibility, prime numbers, and Diophantine equations.

The difficulty of the Final Rounds is comparable to regional competitions like the Arab Mathematical Olympiad (AMO).
